root_idea.summary: The root has two established semantic poles: fear or terror, and seeking or providing aid in a moment of danger.
root_idea.development: Fear gives rise to taking refuge, urgent mobilization, and appeals for succour; the same lexical tradition also preserves the corresponding act of relieving fear and giving aid.

senses.definition: To fear, become frightened, or be terrified.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive verb of entering a state of fear; the feared object may be introduced with مِنْ in the broader lexical construction.

senses.definition: To remove fear from someone; in the Quranic passive construction, for fear to be removed from hearts.
senses.usage_conditions: The attested Quranic construction is passive فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ, with عَنْ marking the removal of fear from the hearts.
In الفَزَعُ الأَكْبَرُ, the expression is explained as the terror associated with entering the Fire; the noun also denotes fear or terror more generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A people's rapid going forth to repel an enemy or comparable threat that has appeared suddenly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional metonymical extension from fear and the urgent response it provokes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or demand aid, succour, refuge, or protection by turning to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially in constructions such as فَزِعَ إِلَيْهِ; the appeal is made because of fear or an affliction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid, succour, or rescue someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use with the opposite relational direction from seeking aid; lexicographic usage includes فَزَعَهُ and فَزِعَ لَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be roused from sleep or to ready oneself through a sudden change of state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of awakening or preparing oneself in response to an event, with the association of fear or alarm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed another in fear or fright.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive comparative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a fearful event or fearful events to befall someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An additionally reported Form II causative use, distinct from removing fear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie with someone in fear or fright and exceed that person therein.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or competitive Form III construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone afraid, frighten, or terrify them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative Form IV use; the feared object or cause may be introduced with مِنْ, مِنْ أَجْلِ, or بِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rouse or awaken someone from sleep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative extension of the state-change use of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid or succour someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV use belonging to the aid branch of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fearful event or occurrence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported nominal extension; its plural is given as أَفْزَاعٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fearful, frightened, terrified, or agitated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a person in fear or disquiet. An extraordinary reported Quran reading uses the form with the sense of being in a state of disquiet, but that reading is not one of the supplied canonical QAC occurrences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Seeking aid or succour, or giving aid or succour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported contrary relational use of the adjective, depending on construction and interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or agency that causes fear or at whom one is frightened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote one by whom, or by means of whom, fear is induced.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single fright or pang of fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression فَزَعَاتُ الرُّوعِ, the fears or frights of the heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who fears people or is often or greatly frightened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal description emphasizing habitual or repeated fear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who frightens people frequently or greatly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive or habitual agent noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or person to which one turns for refuge, protection, preservation, or aid when calamity strikes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Can apply to a place, a person, a group, or other refuge, and is used for one whose aid is sought.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or thing that causes fear or at which one is frightened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative noun distinct from مَفْزَعٌ meaning a refuge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cowardly or easily frightened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explained as being made to fear or frightened at everything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Courageous or secure against fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An opposite, evaluative use applied to one of such courage that fearful events are brought against one like him without overcoming him.

cautions: The aid and succour branch is construction-sensitive: turning to someone in fear means seeking aid, while related transitive constructions can mean giving aid.

The reported extraordinary Quran reading of فَزِعًا in the passage concerning the mother of Moses is preserved as lexical evidence under فَزِعٌ, but it is not assigned a canonical QAC occurrence because that location and morphology are not supplied among the QAC forms.
